course: Business Chinese, Arabic and Russian Translation

lessons.title: Module 4 Lesson 1: Translating African Trade Contracts into Chinese, Arabic and Russian
lessons.body: Welcome to Module 4, Lesson 1 of Business Chinese, Arabic and Russian Translation. This lesson focuses on the high-stakes work of translating African trade contracts into Chinese, Arabic and Russian. Across Africa, contracts are the backbone of cross-border commerce. A cocoa supply agreement between a Ghanaian exporter and a Chinese importer, a construction subcontract between a Kenyan firm and a Russian engineering company, or a logistics deal between a Moroccan freight forwarder and a Gulf investor all depend on precise translation. Your role is not to produce beautiful prose. Your role is to protect your client from financial loss, legal ambiguity and reputational damage. Start with the structure of a standard African trade contract. Most contain parties, recitals, definitions, scope of work, price and payment terms, delivery and Incoterms, inspection, force majeure, dispute resolution, governing law and signatures. Each section carries risk. In Chinese, pay special attention to 甲方 and 乙方, which mean Party A and Party B. These are not always equivalent to buyer and seller. If you translate 甲方 as buyer when the contract defines 甲方 as the seller, you create a fundamental error. In Arabic, watch for الطرف الأول and الطرف الثاني, meaning first party and second party. In Russian, look for Сторона 1 and Сторона 2. Always map the defined terms before translating the body. A practical technique is to build a termbase before you translate a single sentence. For an African coffee export contract to China, your termbase might include FOB Mombasa, phytosanitary certificate, certificate of origin, letter of credit, bill of lading, and quality arbitration. In Chinese, letter of credit is 信用证, bill of lading is 提单, certificate of origin is 原产地证书, and phytosanitary certificate is 植物检疫证书. In Arabic, letter of credit is خطاب اعتماد, bill of lading is بوليصة شحن, certificate of origin is شهادة منشأ, and phytosanitary certificate is شهادة صحة نباتية. In Russian, letter of credit is аккредитив, bill of lading is коносамент, certificate of origin is сертификат происхождения, and phytosanitary certificate is фитосанитарный сертификат. Notice that Russian legal and trade vocabulary often uses loanwords and calques. Do not invent terms. Use the accepted equivalents found in customs documentation and banking practice. Payment terms are the most dangerous area. African exporters frequently negotiate 30 percent advance payment and 70 percent against copy of bill of lading. In Chinese, this may appear as 预付款百分之三十, 余款百分之七十凭提单副本支付. In Arabic, you may see دفعة مقدمة بنسبة 30 بالمائة and 70 بالمائة مقابل نسخة من بوليصة الشحن. In Russian, you may see авансовый платеж 30 процентов and 70 процентов против копии коносамента. A single misplaced percentage or a missing word like copy can change the obligation. Always verify numbers in words and figures. In many African jurisdictions, courts require that amounts be written in words as well as figures. If the source says three hundred thousand US dollars, do not write 300,000 only. Write the words in the target language. In Chinese, use 美元叁拾万元整 or the appropriate formal financial characters. In Arabic, write ثلاثمائة ألف دولار أمريكي. In Russian, write триста тысяч долларов США. Incoterms are another trap. FOB, CIF, CFR, EXW and DAP are standardized, but their explanations differ in local practice. Do not translate FOB as free on board in a way that suggests the seller pays freight. FOB means the seller delivers goods on board the vessel at the named port. In Chinese, keep FOB and add 装运港船上交货. In Arabic, keep FOB and add التسليم على ظهر السفينة في ميناء الشحن. In Russian, keep FOB and add франко-борт. When in doubt, retain the three-letter Incoterm and add a short explanatory gloss. Force majeure is culturally sensitive. African contracts often include force majeure clauses covering floods, drought, strikes, civil unrest and government action. Chinese contracts may use 不可抗力. Arabic contracts may use القوة القاهرة. Russian contracts may use форс-мажор. But the scope differs. A Chinese court may interpret 不可抗力 narrowly, requiring the event to be unforeseeable, unavoidable and insurmountable. An Arabic contract may invoke القوة القاهرة more broadly, including economic hardship. A Russian contract may require notification within a specific period. Your translation must preserve the trigger events, notice periods and consequences. Do not harmonize or simplify. Dispute resolution is equally critical. Many African contracts choose arbitration in Paris, London, Dubai, Singapore or Hong Kong. Chinese parties often prefer CIETAC or HKIAC. Arabic parties may prefer DIAC or the DIFC courts. Russian parties may prefer ICAC at the Chamber of Commerce and Industry of the Russian Federation. When translating an arbitration clause, keep the institution name in its original form and add the target-language equivalent in parentheses. For example, Singapore International Arbitration Centre may be rendered in Chinese as 新加坡国际仲裁中心, in Arabic as مركز سنغافورة الدولي للتحكيم, and in Russian as Сингапурский международный арбитражный центр. Never translate the name of an institution into a different institution. Finally, signatures and seals matter. In China, the company seal, or 公章, often carries more weight than a signature. In many Arab countries, a commercial register extract and a chamber of commerce attestation may be required. In Russia, a печать, or company seal, is still used alongside signatures. When translating signature blocks, include the title, company name, commercial registration number and date. Do not omit the date format. In Africa, dates may be written as 12 March 2025, 12/03/2025 or 2025/03/12. In Chinese, use 2025年3月12日. In Arabic, use 12 مارس 2025. In Russian, use 12 марта 2025 года. Always spell out the month to avoid confusion. Your practical workflow for this lesson is simple. First, read the entire contract before translating. Second, build a termbase with parties, amounts, dates, Incoterms and institutions. Third, translate clause by clause, preserving numbering. Fourth, run a numbers check. Fifth, run a defined-term check. Sixth, have a second reviewer verify names, amounts and dates. Seventh, deliver a clean bilingual or trilingual file with a translator certificate if required. Remember, in African trade, trust is built on accuracy. A mistranslated payment term can delay a shipment in Mombasa, freeze funds in Guangzhou, block a letter of credit in Dubai or trigger a penalty in Moscow. Your precision is your client's protection.

lessons.title: Module 4 Lesson 2: Business Correspondence and Email Translation for African Markets
lessons.body: Welcome to Module 4, Lesson 2. This lesson covers business correspondence and email translation for African markets into Chinese, Arabic and Russian. Email remains the primary tool for negotiating prices, confirming orders, resolving complaints and maintaining relationships across Africa, Asia, the Middle East and Russia. Unlike contracts, emails are shorter, faster and more relational. Your translation must preserve tone, hierarchy and intent. A rude email can destroy a deal. An overly casual email can insult a senior partner. Start with the standard structure of a business email in Africa. Most contain a subject line, salutation, opening courtesy, context, request or response, deadline, closing courtesy, signature and attachments. In Chinese, the subject line should be concise and specific. Instead of Update, write 关于订单号 12345 的发货更新. In Arabic, write تحديث بشأن أمر الشراء رقم 12345. In Russian, write Обновление по заказу номер 12345. Always include the reference number in the subject line. African buyers and sellers often manage dozens of active orders, and a missing reference number causes delays. Salutations are hierarchical. In Chinese, use 尊敬的 for respected, followed by the title and surname. For example, 尊敬的王经理 means Respected Manager Wang. Do not use first names unless you have an established relationship. In Arabic, use السيد المحترم for respected Mr. and السيدة المحترمة for respected Ms., followed by the full name. In Russian, use Уважаемый for respected Mr. and Уважаемая for respected Ms., followed by the first name and patronymic. For example, Уважаемый Иван Петрович. Never use ty in Russian business email. Always use вы. In Arabic, use حضرتك for you when addressing a senior person. In Chinese, use 您 instead of 你. These small choices signal respect. Openings should be warm but not excessive. In African business culture, greetings often include a reference to health, family or the previous conversation. In Chinese, a common opening is 您好, 希望您一切顺利, meaning Hello, I hope all is well with you. In Arabic, a common opening is أتمنى أن تكون بخير, meaning I hope you are well. In Russian, a common opening is Надеюсь, у вас всё хорошо, meaning I hope everything is fine with you. After the opening, state the purpose in the first or second sentence. Do not bury the request. Chinese readers expect the main point early. Arabic readers appreciate a courteous build-up but still want clarity. Russian readers prefer directness with formal politeness. Requests should be explicit. Instead of Please send the documents, write Please send the original bill of lading, commercial invoice and packing list by 20 March 2025. In Chinese, write 请于2025年3月20日前寄送正本提单、商业发票和装箱单. In Arabic, write يرجى إرسال بوليصة الشحن الأصلية والفاتورة التجارية وقائمة التعبئة بحلول 20 مارس 2025. In Russian, write Пожалуйста, отправьте оригинал коносамента, коммерческий инвойс и упаковочный лист до 20 марта 2025 года. Notice that Chinese uses 请, Arabic uses يرجى, and Russian uses Пожалуйста. These are standard polite request markers. Deadlines must be unambiguous. In Africa, time zones range from GMT to GMT plus three. In China, the standard is GMT plus eight. In the Gulf, it is GMT plus three or four. In Russia, it ranges from GMT plus two to GMT plus twelve. Always specify the time zone. Instead of by Friday, write by Friday 21 March 2025, 17:00 Nairobi time, which is GMT plus three. In Chinese, add 内罗毕时间下午5点. In Arabic, add بتوقيت نيروبي الخامسة مساء. In Russian, add по времени Найроби, 17:00. This prevents missed deadlines. Apologies require care. In African business culture, a direct apology is expected when a mistake occurs. In Chinese, use 非常抱歉 for very sorry and 给您带来不便, 敬请谅解 for we apologize for the inconvenience. In Arabic, use نعتذر بشدة for we sincerely apologize and نأسف للإزعاج for we regret the inconvenience. In Russian, use Приносим свои извинения for we apologize and Сожалеем о доставленных неудобствах for we regret the inconvenience caused. Do not over-apologize in Russian or Chinese, as it may be seen as weakness or lack of confidence. One apology followed by a solution is best. Complaints should be factual and solution-oriented. Instead of You sent the wrong goods, write The shipment received on 10 March 2025 contained item A instead of item B as per order 12345. In Chinese, write 2025年3月10日收到的货物中, 第12345号订单的B商品被替换为A商品. In Arabic, write تحتوي الشحنة المستلمة في 10 مارس 2025 على الصنف A بدلاً من الصنف B وفقاً للطلب رقم 12345. In Russian, write В поставке, полученной 10 марта 2025 года, товар A был поставлен вместо товара B согласно заказу номер 12345. Then propose a remedy. In Chinese, 请确认是否补发或退款. In Arabic, يرجى تأكيد ما إذا كان سيتم الإرسال البديل أو استرداد المبلغ. In Russian, Пожалуйста, подтвердите, будет ли произведена замена или возврат средств. This keeps the relationship intact. Closings should match the level of formality. In Chinese, use 此致敬礼 for sincerely, 谢谢 for thanks, or 期待您的回复 for looking forward to your reply. In Arabic, use مع خالص التقدير for with sincere appreciation, وتفضلوا بقبول فائق الاحترام for please accept my highest respect, or في انتظار ردكم for awaiting your reply. In Russian, use С уважением for sincerely, Заранее благодарю for thank you in advance, or Жду вашего ответа for awaiting your reply. Signatures should include full name, title, company, phone, email and WhatsApp number. WhatsApp is widely used in Africa, the Gulf and Russia. In China, WeChat is more common. Include both when possible. Attachments should be listed in the body. In Chinese, write 附件包括. In Arabic, write المرفقات تشمل. In Russian, write Во вложении. Name each file clearly. Avoid vague names like document1.pdf. Use Order12345_Invoice_20250312.pdf. Follow-up emails should be polite but persistent. In Chinese, use 跟进 for follow up. In Arabic, use متابعة. In Russian, use напоминание. A good follow-up says I am following up on my email of 12 March 2025 regarding order 12345. In Chinese, 我就2025年3月12日关于第12345号订单的邮件进行跟进. In Arabic, أتابع بريدي الإلكتروني بتاريخ 12 مارس 2025 بخصوص الطلب رقم 12345. In Russian, Напоминаю о моем письме от 12 марта 2025 года по заказу номер 12345. Then restate the request and deadline. Do not accuse. Do not use all caps. Do not use multiple exclamation marks. Cultural notes are essential. In Chinese business email, hierarchy matters. CC the senior person only when necessary. In Arabic business email, relationship building may take longer. Do not rush to business in the first line. In Russian business email, formal structure and correct titles are important. Use господин for Mr. and госпожа for Ms. when appropriate. In all three languages, avoid sarcasm, irony and humor in serious business correspondence. They rarely translate well. Your practical workflow is to read the email, identify the sender, recipient, relationship, purpose, request, deadline and tone. Then draft in the target language using standard formulas. Then check names, numbers, dates and attachments. Then read aloud to test tone. Then send. If the email is sensitive, ask a native-speaking colleague to review. In African trade, email is not just communication. It is a record. It can be used in arbitration. Write every email as if it may be read in a dispute. That mindset will make your translations accurate, professional and protective.

lessons.title: Module 4 Lesson 3: Translating Business Presentations and Negotiation Documents for African Delegations
lessons.body: Welcome to Module 4, Lesson 3. This lesson covers business presentations and negotiation documents for African delegations working with Chinese, Arabic and Russian counterparts. Presentations are used in trade missions, investment summits, mining conferences, agricultural expos, infrastructure roadshows and banking forums. Negotiation documents include term sheets, memoranda of understanding, letters of intent, pricing schedules and concession agreements. Your translation must be clear, persuasive and culturally appropriate. Start with the presentation deck. African delegations often present investment opportunities in sectors such as energy, mining, agriculture, logistics, fintech, tourism and manufacturing. A typical slide contains a title, bullet points, a chart, a map and a call to action. Your job is to translate the text, not redesign the slide. But you must adapt for length. Chinese is usually shorter than English. Arabic is often longer. Russian is variable. If the English bullet is three words, the Chinese may be two characters, the Arabic may be five words and the Russian may be four words. Plan for font size and line breaks. Do not shrink text below 18 point. Do not overcrowd. Titles should be action-oriented. Instead of Investment Opportunities, write Why Invest in Ghana's Cocoa Sector Now. In Chinese, write 为何现在投资加纳可可产业. In Arabic, write لماذا الاستثمار في قطاع الكاكاو في غانا الآن. In Russian, write Почему стоит инвестировать в какао-сектор Ганы сейчас. This is more persuasive. Numbers must be consistent. If a chart shows 12 percent growth, the text must say 12 percent, not 10 percent. In Chinese, use 增长百分之十二. In Arabic, use نمو بنسبة 12 بالمائة. In Russian, use рост на 12 процентов. Always check the decimal separator. In many African countries, the decimal is a point. In Russia and some Arab countries, the decimal is a comma. In Chinese, the decimal is a point. Do not mix. If the source says 3.5 billion, write 35亿 in Chinese, 3.5 مليار in Arabic and 3,5 миллиарда in Russian. Currency must be explicit. Do not write dollars. Write US dollars, euros, Chinese yuan, UAE dirham, Russian ruble or South African rand. In Chinese, write 美元, 欧元, 人民币, 迪拉姆, 卢布 or 兰特. In Arabic, write دولار أمريكي, يورو, يوان صيني, درهم إماراتي, روبل روسي or راند جنوب أفريقي. In Russian, write доллар США, евро, китайский юань, дирхам ОАЭ, российский рубль or южноафриканский рэнд. Maps require care. Do not translate place names incorrectly. Use the official target-language names. For example, Côte d'Ivoire is 科特迪瓦 in Chinese, ساحل العاج in Arabic and Кот-д'Ивуар in Russian. Do not use Ivory Coast unless the source uses it. For disputed territories, follow the client's instruction and the official position of the target country. This is not a political statement. It is a professional necessity. Charts and graphs need alt text for accessibility and for translation review. If the chart is an image, provide a separate table with the data. Translate the table, not the image. This ensures accuracy. Now consider negotiation documents. A term sheet is shorter than a contract but carries moral and sometimes legal weight. Key terms include valuation, equity split, board seats, dividend policy, exit rights, governing law and exclusivity. In Chinese, valuation is 估值, equity split is 股权分配, board seats is 董事会席位, dividend policy is 分红政策, exit rights is 退出权, governing law is 管辖法律 and exclusivity is 排他性. In Arabic, valuation is التقييم, equity split is تقسيم الأسهم, board seats is مقاعد مجلس الإدارة, dividend policy is سياسة توزيع الأرباح, exit rights is حقوق الخروج, governing law is القانون الحاكم and exclusivity is الحصرية. In Russian, valuation is оценка, equity split is распределение долей, board seats is места в совете директоров, dividend policy is дивидендная политика, exit rights is права на выход, governing law is применимое право and exclusivity is эксклюзивность. Memoranda of understanding are often non-binding, but the language must still be precise. In Chinese, use 谅解备忘录 for memorandum of understanding and 不具约束力 for non-binding. In Arabic, use مذكرة تفاهم and غير ملزمة. In Russian, use меморандум о взаимопонимании and не имеет обязательной силы. Do not translate non-binding as binding by mistake. That single error can create legal liability. Letters of intent are similar. They express intent to proceed, subject to due diligence and board approval. In Chinese, use 意向书. In Arabic, use خطاب نوايا. In Russian, use письмо о намерениях. Include the conditions clearly. Negotiation itself requires interpreting spoken language, but this lesson focuses on documents. Still, you may be asked to prepare talking points. Talking points should be short, numbered and easy to read aloud. In Chinese, use 要点. In Arabic, use نقاط الحديث. In Russian, use тезисы. Each point should be one sentence. Avoid complex clauses. For example, point one: We offer a 10-year tax holiday for mining projects above 500 million US dollars. In Chinese, 我们为5亿美元以上的矿业项目提供10年免税期. In Arabic, نقدم إعفاءً ضريبياً لمدة 10 سنوات لمشاريع التعدين التي تتجاوز 500 مليون دولار أمريكي. In Russian, Мы предлагаем 10-летние налоговые каникулы для горнодобывающих проектов стоимостью более 500 миллионов долларов США. This is clear and memorable. Cultural notes for presentations. In Chinese business culture, presentations should show respect for hierarchy, long-term commitment and government support. Include references to policy alignment, such as Belt and Road Initiative or Forum on China-Africa Cooperation. In Arabic business culture, presentations should emphasize trust, personal relationships and halal compliance if relevant. Include references to the UAE, Saudi Arabia or Qatar as gateways. In Russian business culture, presentations should emphasize technical specifications, timelines and state support. Include references to the Eurasian Economic Union or Russian export centers. In African contexts, presentations should highlight local content, job creation, community development and environmental protection. These are not optional. They are expected. Your practical workflow is to receive the deck and documents, confirm the target language or languages, build a glossary of sector terms, translate slide by slide, check numbers and names, adapt for length, review with a native speaker, and deliver in editable format. If you are interpreting live, prepare a bilingual glossary and practice aloud. In African trade negotiations, the translator is often the only person who understands both sides. Your accuracy can unlock investment, create jobs and build bridges. Your carelessness can kill a deal. Treat every presentation as a chance to build trust.

lessons.title: Module 4 Lesson 4: Translating Financial, Banking and Payment Documents for African Cross-Border Trade
lessons.body: Welcome to Module 4, Lesson 4. This lesson covers financial, banking and payment documents for African cross-border trade with Chinese, Arabic and Russian partners. These documents include letters of credit, bank guarantees, invoices, packing lists, bills of lading, insurance certificates, certificates of origin, inspection certificates and payment instructions. Errors here can delay payment for weeks, trigger penalties or freeze goods at port. Start with the letter of credit, or LC. In Chinese, it is 信用证. In Arabic, it is خطاب اعتماد. In Russian, it is аккредитив. An LC is a bank's promise to pay upon presentation of compliant documents. The key rule is strict compliance. A missing comma can cause rejection. When translating an LC, preserve every field exactly. The applicant is the buyer. The beneficiary is the seller. In Chinese, applicant is 申请人 and beneficiary is 受益人. In Arabic, applicant is مقدم الطلب and beneficiary is المستفيد. In Russian, applicant is заявитель and beneficiary is бенефициар. Do not confuse them. The issuing bank is 开证行 in Chinese, البنك المصدر in Arabic and банк-эмитент in Russian. The advising bank is 通知行 in Chinese, البنك المُبلغ in Arabic and авизующий банк in Russian. The negotiating bank is 议付行 in Chinese, البنك المفاوض in Arabic and негоциирующий банк in Russian. The confirming bank is 保兑行 in Chinese, البنك المؤكد in Arabic and подтверждающий банк in Russian. Keep these terms consistent across all documents. Payment terms must match the LC. If the LC says payment at sight, write 即期付款 in Chinese, الدفع عند الاطلاع in Arabic and оплата по предъявлении in Russian. If it says 90 days after bill of lading date, write 提单日后90天付款 in Chinese, الدفع بعد 90 يوماً من تاريخ بوليصة الشحن in Arabic and оплата через 90 дней после даты коносамента in Russian. Do not change the trigger event. A common error is translating after bill of lading date as after shipment date. These are not always the same. The bill of lading date is the date the goods were loaded on board. The shipment date may be earlier or later. Always use the exact wording. Invoices must match the LC description of goods. If the LC says 100 metric tons of Arabica coffee beans, grade A, crop year 2024, the invoice must say the same. In Chinese, write 100公吨A级2024年产阿拉比卡咖啡豆. In Arabic, write 100 طن متري من حبوب البن العربي درجة أ، محصول عام 2024. In Russian, write 100 метрических тонн кофейных зерен арабика, сорт A, урожай 2024 года. Do not add or remove words. Do not use synonyms. The bank checks the description against the LC. A mismatch is a discrepancy. Packing lists must show the number of packages, the type of package, the gross weight, the net weight and the dimensions. In Chinese, use 件数, 包装类型, 毛重, 净重 and 尺寸. In Arabic, use عدد الطرود, نوع العبوة, الوزن الإجمالي, الوزن الصافي and الأبعاد. In Russian, use количество мест, тип упаковки, вес брутто, вес нетто and размеры. Do not round numbers. If the source says 1,234.56 kilograms, write 1,234.56公斤 in Chinese, 1,234.56 كيلوغرام in Arabic and 1 234,56 килограмма in Russian. Note the Russian decimal comma and space separator. Bills of lading are critical. The shipper, consignee, notify party, port of loading, port of discharge, vessel name, voyage number, container number, seal number and freight terms must be exact. In Chinese, shipper is 托运人, consignee is 收货人, notify party is 通知方, port of loading is 装货港, port of discharge is 卸货港, vessel is 船名, voyage is 航次, container is 集装箱, seal is 封条 and freight is 运费. In Arabic, shipper is الشاحن, consignee is المرسل إليه, notify party is الطرف المطلوب إخطاره, port of loading is ميناء التحميل, port of discharge is ميناء التفريغ, vessel is اسم السفينة, voyage is رقم الرحلة, container is الحاوية, seal is الختم and freight is الشحن. In Russian, shipper is грузоотправитель, consignee is грузополучатель, notify party is уведомляемая сторона, port of loading is порт погрузки, port of discharge is порт выгрузки, vessel is название судна, voyage is номер рейса, container is контейнер, seal is пломба and freight is фрахт. A single wrong digit in a container number can send goods to the wrong port. Insurance certificates must show the insured amount, the currency, the risks covered and the claims payable location. In Chinese, use 保险金额, 币种, 承保风险 and 赔付地点. In Arabic, use مبلغ التأمين, العملة, المخاطر المغطاة and مكان دفع المطالبات. In Russian, use страховая сумма, валюта, покрытые риски and место выплаты страхового возмещения. Most African trade insurance is in US dollars, euros or rand. Do not convert currencies unless instructed. Certificates of origin must match the rules of origin in the trade agreement. For example, under the African Continental Free Trade Area, or AfCFTA, goods must meet specific local content thresholds. In Chinese, AfCFTA is 非洲大陆自由贸易区. In Arabic, it is منطقة التجارة الحرة القارية الأفريقية. In Russian, it is Африканская континентальная зона свободной торговли. If the certificate says wholly obtained, write 完全获得 in Chinese, تم الحصول عليها بالكامل in Arabic and полностью произведенные in Russian. If it says sufficiently worked or processed, write 充分加工 in Chinese, تم تصنيعها بشكل كافٍ in Arabic and достаточно переработанные in Russian. Do not guess. Inspection certificates from SGS, Bureau Veritas or Intertek must be translated carefully. The inspection date, the inspection location, the standard used and the result must be exact. In Chinese, use 检验日期, 检验地点, 检验标准和 检验结果. In Arabic, use تاريخ الفحص, مكان الفحص, المعيار المستخدم and النتيجة. In Russian, use дата инспекции, место инспекции, использованный стандарт and результат. Payment instructions must include the SWIFT code, IBAN, account number, account name, bank name, bank address and correspondent bank. In Chinese, SWIFT code is 环球银行金融电信协会代码, IBAN is 国际银行账号, account number is 账号, account name is 账户名称, bank name is 银行名称 and correspondent bank is 代理行. In Arabic, SWIFT code is رمز سويفت, IBAN is رقم الحساب المصرفي الدولي, account number is رقم الحساب, account name is اسم الحساب, bank name is اسم البنك and correspondent bank is البنك المراسل. In Russian, SWIFT code is код SWIFT, IBAN is международный номер банковского счета, account number is номер счета, account name is наименование счета, bank name is наименование банка and correspondent bank is банк-корреспондент. One wrong digit in an IBAN can send funds to the wrong account. Always verify with the client. Sanctions compliance is a growing issue. Chinese, Arabic and Russian banks may have different sanctions policies. Do not translate sanctions language loosely. If a document says sanctioned person, write 受制裁人员 in Chinese, شخص خاضع للعقوبات in Arabic and лицо, находящееся под санкциями in Russian. If it says frozen assets, write 冻结资产 in Chinese, أصول مجمدة in Arabic and замороженные активы in Russian. If you are unsure, ask the client for the exact legal reference. Your practical workflow is to receive the document set, identify the LC or payment method, build a field-by-field checklist, translate each field, verify numbers and names against the source, check consistency across documents, and deliver with a discrepancy report. In African cross-border trade, the bank does not care about beautiful language. The bank cares about exact compliance. Your precision is the difference between payment and delay. Treat every field as if it is the only field.

lessons.title: Module 4 Lesson 5: Quality Assurance, Cultural Mediation and Professional Ethics in African Business Translation
lessons.body: Welcome to Module 4, Lesson 5. This lesson covers quality assurance, cultural mediation and professional ethics in African business translation into Chinese, Arabic and Russian. By now you have practiced contracts, correspondence, presentations and financial documents. This final lesson ties everything together. It is about how to deliver reliable work, how to mediate cultural differences and how to behave ethically when the stakes are high. Start with quality assurance. A professional translation workflow has five stages: preparation, translation, revision, review and finalization. Preparation means reading the source, confirming the target language, identifying the audience, building a termbase and clarifying ambiguities with the client. Translation means producing a complete draft without skipping sections. Revision means checking accuracy, completeness, grammar, spelling and consistency. Review means having a second qualified translator or subject matter expert check the work. Finalization means formatting, proof

quiz.q: Which greeting is most appropriate in a formal business email in Chinese?
quiz.explanation: 您好 is the polite formal greeting used in business correspondence, while the others are casual or inappropriate.

quiz.q: In Arabic business correspondence, which phrase is commonly used to open a formal letter?
quiz.explanation: تحية طيبة وبعد is a standard formal opening meaning greetings and to proceed, suitable for business letters.

quiz.q: Which Russian form of address is most suitable for a business letter to an unknown company?
quiz.explanation: Уважаемые господа means Dear Sirs and is the standard formal business salutation in Russian.

quiz.q: When translating a Chinese business card, which element usually appears first in the translated version for Western readers?
quiz.explanation: For Western readers, the personal name is typically placed first, followed by title and company details.

quiz.q: Which Arabic term is commonly used for a limited liability company?
quiz.explanation: شركة ذات مسؤولية محدودة translates as limited liability company, a common business entity type.

quiz.q: In Russian business documents, what does the abbreviation ООО stand for?
quiz.explanation: ООО stands for Общество с ограниченной ответственностью, meaning limited liability company.

quiz.q: Which Chinese term is the standard translation for the business concept of due diligence?
quiz.explanation: 尽职调查 is the established Chinese business term for due diligence in mergers and acquisitions.

quiz.q: When translating a formal Russian business letter into Arabic, which closing is most appropriate?
quiz.explanation: وتفضلوا بقبول فائق الاحترام is a highly formal Arabic closing equivalent to please accept my highest respect.
